A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same LP-DS research work. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and complete Appendices A–G are readable and support comparison; the shorter v2 retains the appendix material.

before.justification: V1 reports original benchmark experiments, diversity analyses, ablations, and physical Franka evaluations, including numerical outcomes in Tables 5–6.

after.justification: V2 retains these original experimental results, including simulation benchmarks and physical-robot success counts.

M1.justification: The specified residual changes from state-only Δθ(s) to state-and-noise-conditioned Δθ(s, ε). Section 4.1 and Algorithm 1 propagate this additional input through action generation, next-state targets, and actor/dual updates. This substantially expands the transformation beyond a state-dependent Gaussian translation, although the PDFs do not establish whether the experimental implementation changed.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same RoboMimic, Gym, Adroit, symmetric toy-navigation, AVOIDING, LIBERO-90 cream-cheese, and physical Franka tasks. No dataset, task, or test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: Figure 3 retains DSRL, DPPO, IDQL, and DQL. Comparator membership also remains unchanged in the other experiments, including frozen-backbone comparisons and the LP-DS-A action-space ablation.

E3.justification: Section 5 and Appendices A–G retain the same backbone assignments, evaluation metrics, decoding procedures, hyperparameter settings, interaction budgets, and rollout/trial designs. No experimental protocol revision is reported alongside the method reformulation.

E4.justification: Both versions contain the same mode-coverage and entropy analyses, Lagrangian/clipping ablations, trust-region sweeps, action-space versus noise-space comparison, and diffusion versus flow-matching comparison. Their evidence and tested questions are unchanged.

E5.justification: The stated reporting practice remains mean performance with ±1 standard deviation, six seeds for main benchmarks, and three for entropy analyses and ablations. Appendix A.4 retains identical seeds across methods; no uncertainty procedure is added or revised.

E6.justification: The plotted results and numerical result tables are unchanged. For example, Table 6 reports the same frozen-backbone versus LP-DS successes: 18/40 versus 33/40 for pick-and-place and 11/20 versus 17/20 for mug hanging.

T1.justification: Section 4.2 adds regularity and small-Jacobian conditions to the KL approximation and extends the perturbation expectations to sampled noise. It also removes the misleading 'dual gradient ascent' description. These refine the existing mathematical justification and updates without adding a theorem or proof.

C1.justification: The introduction's contribution statement and the conclusion now characterize LP-DS as learning a state-and-noise-conditioned residual instead of a state-only residual. The main claims about performance, diversity preservation, and applicability across backbones and robotic settings remain unchanged.

C2.justification: V2 replaces Gaussian 'support' and 'off-manifold' explanations with low-prior-density regions. Section 4.2 also changes the assertion of valid operation at every encountered state to closeness to the prior on average over states. These meaningfully qualify the mechanism and constraint interpretation.

D1.justification: Appendices A–G retain the same implementation sources, hyperparameter tables, data-generation instructions, simulator and sensor details, and deployment procedures. Project-page and video-access information are also unchanged.

R1.justification: The cited works and bibliography are unchanged. Despite compressing the opening related-work paragraph, v2 retains the same positioning against prior-replacing DSRL and generation-focused noise-amortization approaches.

P1.justification: V2 shortens the opening related-work paragraph and revises terminology throughout the introduction, methodology, and conclusion to reflect noise conditioning and more precise prior-density language. The overall section organization and experimental narrative remain intact.

P2.justification: Figure 2's caption is revised, equations and Algorithm 1 reflow, and tighter pagination absorbs v1's nearly empty final reference page. All figures and tables are retained; their graphics and table structures are unchanged.

improvement.justification: V2 improves precision by qualifying the KL approximation and replacing per-state and Gaussian-support language. However, it changes the central residual definition while retaining all experimental results, without explaining whether noise conditioning corrects an earlier description or changes the evaluated implementation. This unresolved connection between the revised method and retained evidence prevents a reliable net quality judgment.
